newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end mixed after trade data.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end mixed after trade data.

text.p: Singapore shares ended mixed on Friday after the release of November trade data where non-oil domestic exports saw an unexpected sharp fall of 8.8 percent.
"The market is a bit mixed. It was quite strong in the morning but fell at noon after the trade numbers," said a broker with a local firm.

She said some stocks managed to recover in the afternoon. "There is a bit of window dressing going on with Christmas and New Year holidays coming up." The Straits Times Industrial index ended 2.54 points lower at 2,196.81. Volume was 107.9 million with 168 gainers and 153 losers.
Another dealer said some funds fleeing Thailand's plunging stockmarket have made their way into the Singapore market.

Topping the actives list continued to be Malaysia's speculative Berjaya Group with almost 15 million traded. It ended up four cents at S$1.14. Index stock NatSteel rose to hit a new year high of S$3.18 before easing to close at S$3.14, up 14 cents on active volume of 4.36 million.

Singapore Telecom lost four cents to S$3.18 on speculation that it is under pressure to lower rates. Singapore Press, Clipsal and UOB foreign ended higher while Cycle & Carriage and City Developments were lower. - Doreen Siow 65-8703080
